Markets increased bets on rate hikes after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish speech and Middle East tensions flared again. Meanwhile, the yen hovered near the closely watched 160‑yen‑per‑dollar threshold.
In New York's late session, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, fell 0.29% to 99.41.

Warsh said last Friday that if policymakers cannot gain enough confidence that inflation is moving toward the 2% target, the Fed still has work to do. This is his clearest statement yet, implying that the Fed may need to tighten policy further to curb price pressure.

The remarks lifted expectations of a September rate hike. Market odds that the Fed will raise rates next month have risen to 60%. The 2‑year U.S. Treasury yield, highly sensitive to rates, remains just below a one‑month high.

Rabobank macro strategy head Elwin de Groot said, "Warsh's pre‑planned remarks seem designed to boost market expectations of a rate hike, shift September policy debate back to the hawk side, and restore his credibility in fighting inflation."
He added, "Warsh sent an important signal: the Fed will not rely solely on tightening the financial environment to curb inflation; if core inflation stalls, the Fed is willing to tighten further."

Investors are now focusing on upcoming U.S. economic data, especially the non‑farm payrolls due Friday and next week’s consumer inflation data. Both could influence market expectations for the September Fed meeting.
The dollar index has fallen for a second consecutive month, as the Treasury’s earlier repurchase plan this month sparked renewed dollar‑depreciation bets.
The euro rose 0.16% to 1 euro = 1.1602 dollars. The pound also edged higher to 1 pound = 1.3543 dollars. Both currencies have risen for a second consecutive month.

Meanwhile, Middle East tensions have risen again, pushing oil higher. Markets will next watch the G20 finance ministers and central bank governors meeting hosted by the U.S. on Monday and Tuesday. Investors will look for coordinated action, severing ties with Iran, and measures to ease concerns about U.S. debt growth and Treasury yields.

The persistently weak yen remains a market focus. The yen rose about 0.24% to 159.65 yen per dollar, after falling below 160 yen per dollar on Friday. The 160 threshold is widely seen as a key level that could raise Japan’s official intervention risk, prompting renewed attention to whether Tokyo and Washington might act again to support the yen.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that the yen’s recent moves are "well‑controlled" and that he expects Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda to make the "right decision" on monetary policy.
UBP Asia senior economist Carlos Casanova said, "Historically, currency market intervention only works when fundamentals move in the same direction."
He noted, "The yen still faces multiple pressures, including a large interest‑rate differential, negative real rates, and the BoJ’s cautious pace of action."

items.title_en: TWD, Stocks and FX Both Slip, Closing at 31.666, August Still Rallied 0.626
paras: 台北股匯今 (31) 日同步走弱，受到熱錢流出影響，新台幣兌美元匯率一度貶破 31.7 元關卡，不過，適逢出口商月底拋匯需求，加上央行出手調節，帶動新台幣貶勢收斂，終場收在 31.666 元，貶值 3.8 分，台北與元太外匯市場總成交值 35.505 億美元。
回顧新台幣匯率 8 月表現，全月強升 6.26 角、升幅 1.94%，月線由黑翻紅。
新台幣兌美元今天開盤價為 31.65 元，盤中最高來到 31.6 元、最低下探 31.732 元。
MSCI 最新季度調整於今天盤後生效，台股今天一度重挫逾 880 點，電子族群普遍賣壓沉重，不過，金融股逆勢撐盤，加上大立光帶動部分共同封裝光學(CPO)概念股走強，指數跌幅逐漸收斂，終場下跌202.98點，收 46128.47 點。台股8月強彈3008.72點，漲幅6.98%，月線收紅。
觀察主要貨幣今天對美元表現，根據央行統計，美元指數上漲 0.31%，新台幣貶值 0.12%，星幣貶值 0.17%，日元小貶 0.04%，而韓元逆勢升值 0.25%，人民幣微升 0.01%，主要亞幣走勢不同調。
美國聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)在傑克森霍爾(Jackson Hole)會議發表首次主題演講後，市場認為其立場偏向鷹派。華許表示，美國潛在通膨趨勢並未「明顯改善」，交易員因此提高對聯準會(Fed)9月升息的預期。美元已升至近兩周高點。
paras_en: Taipei’s stock and foreign‑exchange markets weakened in tandem on the 31st, as hot‑money outflows pushed the New Taiwan dollar past the 31.7 per USD barrier. However, exporters dumped foreign currency at month‑end and the central bank intervened, curbing the depreciation. The TWD settled at 31.666 per USD, down 0.038, with total FX turnover reaching US$35.505 billion.
Looking back at the TWD’s performance in August, the currency surged the whole month by 0.626 NTD (1.94%), turning the monthly trend line from black to red.
The TWD opened today at 31.65 per USD, hit an intraday high of 31.60 and fell to a low of 31.732.

MSCI’s latest quarterly rebalancing took effect after today’s close. The Taiwan index once plunged more than 880 points, with the electronics sector under heavy selling pressure. Financial stocks provided support, and a rally in Largan Precision lifted some CPO‑related stocks, narrowing the decline. The index finished down 202.98 points at 46,128.47. In August the market bounced back 3,008.72 points, up 6.98%, closing the month in the green.

Among major currencies versus the dollar, the US Dollar Index rose 0.31%, the TWD slipped 0.12%, the Singapore dollar fell 0.17%, the yen weakened 0.04%, the Korean won appreciated 0.25%, and the Chinese yuan edged up 0.01%, showing divergent moves among Asian currencies.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, speaking at the Jackson Hole conference, delivered his first keynote and was perceived as hawkish. Warsh said the US underlying inflation trend has not “clearly improved,” prompting traders to raise expectations for a Fed rate hike in September. The dollar rose to near a two‑week high.

items.title: 日元貶破160防線 當局隨時突襲干預、緊盯兩個關鍵價位
items.title_en: Yen Breaks 160 Barrier, Authorities Ready to Intervene at Key Levels
paras: 日元兌美元貶破160防線，凸顯出日元極易受到進一步走貶的衝擊，也大幅提高日本當局再次進場干預、阻貶匯率的風險。
儘管確切干預門檻仍不明朗，但多名策略師周一(31日)警告，可能促使當局出手阻止日元急貶的價位不少，最近的觀察點從161開始，其次是162至163區間。不過，他們仍認為，干預行動頂多只能爭取時間，因為日元已回吐7月底展開史上最大規模干預以來逾半數漲幅。
日元最新一波跌勢，主要受到美元上周五全面走強帶動，市場預期美國利率將維持在更高水準，也進一步印證日元走勢很大程度並非日本所能掌控。
日本7月進場干預後，日元未能升破155，隨後再度承壓。當時美國與日本聯手買進日元，是雙方自1998年以來首度採取協調干預行動。
三井住友日興證券資深利率與外匯策略師丸山倫斗表示：「就關鍵價位而言，首先要觀察161，其次是162.9至163.3區間，這是當局上次進場干預的位置。」不過，他指出，政府在前一次干預時「相當重視出其不意」，意味當局隨時都可能採取行動。
周一東京時間上午11點50分，日元兌美元匯率報159.77，較上周五紐約收盤價約160.09升值約0.2%。
根據日本財務省數據顯示，日本在過去一個月內砸下創紀錄的964億美元來支撐日元，此前日元曾崩跌至40年來的低點。財務大臣片山皐月與美國財政部長貝森特皆已暗示，必要時願意再次採取行動。
日本官員多次表明，評估是否有必要干預的關鍵在於匯率變動的速度與失序程度，而非任何特定的匯價水準。
貝森特也曾表示，他期望日本央行總裁植田和男能在貨幣政策上「做出正確的事」，同時形容近期日元的波動「相當受到控制」。
交換市場定價顯示，日本銀行在9月18日政策會議前升息的機率達90%，市場更已完全反映最晚10月30日前升息的預期。
澳洲國民銀行策略師Rodrigo Catril表示：「我們認為，美元兌日元升破162後，干預風險才會明顯升高。當美元全面走強，加上聯準會釋出鷹派訊號時，日本很難出手干預。」
投機性部位也再度轉向不利日元。避險基金在干預後一度大幅削減看空部位，如今又開始建立日元空單。自2025年7月以來，避險基金整體上一直對日元抱持負面看法。
澳洲聯邦銀行策略師Carol Kong表示：「如果日元快速貶值，我不認為日本當局一定要等到日本銀行開會後才再度干預。不過，由於市場已高度反映9月升息的可能性，當局或許會傾向先觀察貨幣政策能否發揮部分支撐日元的效果。」
市場人士指出，只要日本實質利率仍處於深度負值，單靠干預恐怕難以扭轉日元走勢。
華僑銀行策略師Moh Siong Sim認為，鑑於市場預期的升息幅度有限，日本央行正陷入更大的兩難。看來勢必得祭出鼓勵資金回流等其他政策工具，才能扭轉日元疲弱的頹勢。
paras_en: The yen fell below the 160 barrier against the dollar, highlighting its vulnerability to further depreciation and significantly raising the risk of Japanese authorities stepping in to curb the decline.

Although the exact intervention threshold remains unclear, several strategists warned on Monday (31st) that intervention could be triggered at several levels, starting at 161 and then the 162‑163 range. They still believe intervention would only buy time, as the yen has already reversed more than half of the gains since the largest intervention in history at the end of July.

The latest yen selloff was mainly driven by a comprehensive strengthening of the dollar last Friday, with markets expecting U.S. rates to remain higher, further confirming that the yen’s trajectory is largely beyond Japan’s control.

After Japan intervened in July, the yen failed to break above 155 and was subsequently pressured again. At that time, the U.S. and Japan jointly bought yen, marking the first coordinated intervention since 1998.

Mitsui Sumitomo Nikko Securities senior interest‑rate and FX strategist Tomoaki Maruyama said, "The key levels to watch are first 161, then the 162.9‑163.3 range, where the authorities last intervened." He added that the government placed great emphasis on surprise in the previous intervention, implying that action could be taken at any time.
At 11:50 a.m. Tokyo time on Monday, the yen was quoted at 159.77 against the dollar, about 0.2% stronger than the New York close on Friday at 160.09.

According to data from Japan’s Ministry of Finance, Japan spent a record 96.4 billion dollars in the past month to support the yen, after it had fallen to a 40‑year low. Finance Minister Hitoshi Katayama and U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen have both signaled willingness to act again if necessary.
Japanese officials have repeatedly stated that the key to deciding whether to intervene lies in the speed and disorder of the exchange‑rate movement, not any specific rate level.
Yellen also said she expects Bank of Japan Governor Haruhiko Kuroda to "do the right thing" in monetary policy, describing the recent yen volatility as "quite controlled."
Market pricing in the foreign‑exchange market shows a 90% probability of a rate hike at the BoJ policy meeting on September 18, with the market fully pricing in a hike by October 30 at the latest.

Australia’s National Australia Bank strategist Rodrigo Catril said, "We believe the risk of intervention rises significantly once the dollar rises above 162 against the yen. With the dollar strengthening and the Fed issuing hawkish signals, Japan would find it difficult to intervene."

Speculative positions have again turned against the yen. Hedge funds had previously cut short positions after intervention, but are now re‑building yen shorts. Since July 2025, hedge funds have generally maintained a negative view of the yen.

Australia’s Commonwealth Bank strategist Carol Kong said, "If the yen depreciates rapidly, I don’t think Japan will wait until the BoJ meeting to intervene again. However, since the market already reflects the likelihood of a September hike, authorities may prefer to observe whether monetary policy can provide some support for the yen."
Market participants note that as long as Japan’s real rates remain deeply negative, intervention alone is unlikely to reverse the yen’s trend.

China‑based Bank of China strategist Moh Siong Sim believes that given the limited expected rate hikes, the BoJ is in a deeper dilemma. It appears that other policy tools, such as encouraging capital inflows, will be needed to reverse the yen’s weak trajectory.

據財務省數據顯示，日本當局過去一個月斥資創紀錄的15.4兆日圓干預外匯市場以支撐日圓，規模顯現政府推動日圓擺脫四十年低位的決心，但美國密西根大學調查8月美國消費者對一年通貨膨脹預期降至4.0%，但消費者信心指數終值升至51.7高於預期及對五年期通膨脹預期維持3.3%，而且FED主席沃什在杰克森霍爾經濟研討會上發表演講表示，若決策者無法確信通貨膨脹率正回歸2%目標水平，那麼FED還有工作要做，並承認當前金融狀況未對經濟形成明顯限制，為迄今釋放最接近可能需要進一步升息的訊號，提振美元兌日圓至160.20高點。預估今日美元兌日圓支撐於159.70-90，阻力於160.70-90。

Last week, initial US jobless claims fell for a second consecutive week to a one‑month low, but July's trade deficit hit a 16‑month high. At the Jackson Hole annual economic symposium, Federal Reserve officials expressed concerns about inflation, with many supporting another rate hike. Yet on Friday, before Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s speech at the symposium, the dollar was flat. Meanwhile, Japan reported a July job‑vacancy ratio of 1.18, unemployment fell to 2.4%, and August Tokyo CPI rose 1.8% year‑on‑year, above expectations, with core CPI (excluding food and energy) accelerating to 2.0%. Core inflation has risen for three straight months, strengthening the case for the Bank of Japan to raise rates as early as September. Prime Minister Kishida also said the government plans to cap new government bond issuance at about ¥40 trillion in the FY2027 budget, and Finance Minister Shunichi Suzuki will attend the G20 finance ministers’ meeting on Tuesday, where markets will watch whether he meets US Treasury Secretary Yellen, supporting the dollar/yen hovering near the ¥159.28 low.

According to Ministry of Finance data, Japanese authorities intervened in the FX market with a record ¥15.4 trillion over the past month to support the yen, showing the government’s resolve to lift the yen from four‑decade lows. In the US, the University of Michigan’s August survey showed one‑year inflation expectations falling to 4.0%, while consumer confidence rose to 51.7, above forecasts, and five‑year inflation expectations held at 3.3%. Fed Chair Powell, speaking at Jackson Hole, warned that if policymakers are not convinced inflation is returning to the 2% target, the Fed still has work to do, acknowledging that current financial conditions have not yet imposed a clear drag on the economy. This was the clearest hint yet of possible further rate hikes, pushing the dollar/yen up to a ¥160.20 high. The dollar/yen is expected to find support around ¥159.70‑90 and face resistance near ¥160.70‑90 today.
EUR/USD

Strong Australian inflation and spending data have boosted expectations that the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) will raise rates again soon. At the same time, the three‑year government bond yield hit a one‑month high and the ten‑year yield rose to its highest level since May. The RBA also warned that rates could be raised further. Last Friday the Australian dollar climbed to a three‑month high, and markets see a 96% chance that the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) will hike 25 basis points to 2.75% on Wednesday, lifting the kiwi and pushing the euro/dollar up to a 1.1657 peak.

Data show Germany’s July import prices rose 0.2% from the previous month and 6.8% year‑on‑year, above the prior figures. France reported August CPI and the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) up 2.7% and 2.4% year‑on‑year, respectively. An EU Commission survey in August showed the euro‑area’s economic, industrial and services confidence indices improving to 98.4, –5.3 and 5.8. However, Powell’s hawkish remarks lifted the dollar across the board, pulling the euro/dollar down to a 1.1577 low. The euro/dollar is expected to face resistance at 1.1590‑1.1610 and support at 1.1510‑1.1530 today.
GBP/USD

Last Friday, a Lloyds Bank survey showed UK August business confidence rising to 53, the highest since March, echoing other recent signs of improving economic outlook and supporting the pound at a 1.3598 high against the dollar. As Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said the second‑round inflation effect is relatively mild, and Powell’s hawkish comments boosted the dollar, the pound fell to a 1.3524 low. The pound/dollar is expected to encounter resistance at 1.3545‑1.3565 and support at 1.3450‑1.3480 today.

items.title: 〈紐約匯市〉美元走強本周漲約1% 華許演講提高9月升息預期
items.title_en: NY Forex: Dollar Strengthens, Up About 1% This Week; Warsh Speech Raises September Rate‑Hike Expectations
paras: 美元周五(28日)升至近兩周高點， 美國聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)在傑克森霍爾(Jackson Hole)會議發表首次主題演講後，市場認為其立場偏向鷹派。華許表示，美國潛在通膨趨勢並未「明顯改善」，交易員因此提高對聯準會(Fed)9月升息的預期。
美元本周上漲約1%，收復前一周因美國公債大幅遭拋售、引發所謂「貨幣貶值交易」而蒙受的全部跌幅。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)上漲0.5%，報99.65，為8月18日以來最高。
聯準會主席備受期待的傑克森霍爾年度經濟政策研討會演講，涵蓋從人工智慧(AI)、前瞻指引到當前經濟狀況等議題。值得注意的是，他表示美國潛在通膨趨勢並未「明顯改善」，並再次強調聯準會應將維持價格穩定作為政策重點。
華許演講之際，聯準會正處於複雜局面。近期通膨數據持續偏高，加上美國與伊朗似乎無休止的衝突推升油價，以及非農就業數據意外疲弱，導致聯邦公開市場委員會(FOMC)內部分歧加劇，3位地區聯準銀行總裁反對7月維持利率不變的決定。
華許在事先準備的講稿中表示，「截至目前，我認為勞動市場符合充分就業的狀態。但就我們的價格穩定職責而言，目前的數據更加令人擔憂。」
市場認為這場演講偏鷹，交易員提高對9月升息25個基點的預期。根據CME FedWatch工具，9月升息25個基點的機率目前超過57%，高於前一天約35%。
德銀分析師Matthew Luzzetti率領團隊表示，「華許主席的演講，在對經濟與展望的具體程度，以及明顯偏鷹的立場方面，都令我們感到意外。在他的談話之後，我們認為，除非即將公布的數據大幅低於預期，否則9月升息25個基點的壓力已經落在數據上。反過來，我們仍認為聯準會今年將升息50個基點，分別在9月與12月會議升息。」
貨幣貶值交易退潮 美元回升
華許發表演講後，美國公債殖利率轉為上升，債券遭到拋售。10年期公債殖利率上升5.9個基點至4.729%，對利率較敏感的2年期公債殖利率則上升12個基點至4.352%。
近期債券市場劇烈震盪，長天期公債受到通膨疑慮、企業發債規模龐大，以及美國國債持續膨脹等因素影響而遭拋售。
美國財政部上周出人意料的干預措施，對抑制殖利率上升的效果有限。
一般來說，公債殖利率上升會產生類似升息的效果，因這會推高消費者與企業的借貸成本，通常有利於美元走強。但美國國債突破40兆美元的消息在上周引發市場對財政狀況的疑慮，在此環境下，投資人傾向將資金從法定貨幣轉向黃金或加密貨幣等硬資產，這種策略被稱為「貨幣貶值交易」。
事實上，美元指數上周下跌近1%，而黃金與加密貨幣則上漲。兩者本周也持續上漲，但在美元走強情況下，漲幅明顯較小。
加幣受貿易戰拖累 本周大幅下跌
其他主要貨幣方面，本周加幣受到外匯交易員關注，在華盛頓與渥太華之間的貿易戰升溫之際，加幣下跌1%。
美加兩國上周末談判破裂後，雙方相繼對彼此加徵報復性關稅。美國總統川普周四推動將安大略湖(Lake Ontario)更名為「美國湖」(Lake America)。
加拿大政府周五公布數據顯示，該國經濟第二季強勁反彈，按年率計成長3.3%，明顯高於第一季經上修後的0.3%增幅。這項成長符合經濟學家預期，但遠高於加拿大央行約2.5%的預測。
日元自歷史性干預後首度觸及160
華許發表鷹派演講後，日元周五承受壓力。美元兌日元觸及160，為美日兩國7月底進行歷史性聯合干預以來首次觸及這項水準。160也曾是過去引發干預的關鍵價位。
另一方面，韓元連續第二個交易日兌美元走強，美元兌韓元匯率本周下跌約0.5%。投資人消化韓國央行(BoK)周四連續第二次會議升息的決定後，韓元走強，借貸成本也因此升至18個月高點。

paras_en: The dollar rose on Friday (the 28th) to near a two‑week high after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivered his first thematic speech at the Jackson Hole conference, leading the market to view his stance as hawkish. Warsh said the underlying inflation trend in the United States has not "clearly improved," prompting traders to raise expectations for a September Fed rate hike.
The dollar gained roughly 1% this week, recouping the entire loss it suffered last week when a sharp sell‑off in U.S. Treasuries triggered a so‑called "currency‑devaluation trade."
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, rose 0.5% to 99.65, its highest level since August 18.

The highly anticipated Jackson Hole annual economic policy symposium speech by the Fed chair covered topics ranging from artificial intelligence (AI) and forward guidance to the current economic situation. Notably, he said the underlying inflation trend in the United States has not "clearly improved" and reiterated that the Fed must keep price stability as its policy priority.

Warsh’s speech came as the Fed was navigating a complex environment. Recent inflation data remained elevated, oil prices were pushed higher by the seemingly endless U.S.–Iran conflict, and a surprisingly weak non‑farm payroll report deepened divisions within the Federal Open Market Committee, with three regional Fed presidents opposing the July decision to keep rates unchanged.
In his prepared remarks, Warsh said, "As of now, I believe the labor market is at a level of full employment. But with respect to our price‑stability mandate, the current data are more concerning."

The market interpreted the speech as hawkish, and traders lifted their expectations for a 25‑basis‑point rate hike in September. According to the CME FedWatch tool, the probability of a 25‑bp hike in September is now above 57%, up from roughly 35% the day before.

Deutsche Bank analyst Matthew Luzzetti and his team said, "Chair Warsh’s speech surprised us both in the concreteness of his economic outlook and his clearly hawkish tone. After his remarks we think the pressure for a 25‑bp hike in September now rests on the data, unless upcoming releases come in far below expectations. Conversely, we still expect the Fed to raise rates by 50 bps this year, with hikes at the September and December meetings."
Currency‑devaluation trades receded and the dollar recovered.
After Warsh’s speech, U.S. Treasury yields turned higher and bonds were sold off. The 10‑year yield rose 5.9 bp to 4.729%, while the more rate‑sensitive 2‑year yield jumped 12 bp to 4.352%.

Bond markets have been extremely volatile lately; long‑dated Treasuries have been sold off amid inflation concerns, a large volume of corporate issuance, and the continued expansion of U.S. sovereign debt.
The U.S. Treasury’s unexpected intervention last week had limited effect in curbing the rise in yields.

Generally, higher Treasury yields act like a rate hike by raising borrowing costs for consumers and firms, which usually supports a stronger dollar. However, news that U.S. sovereign debt surpassed $40 trillion last week sparked concerns about fiscal health, prompting investors to shift funds from fiat currencies into hard assets such as gold or cryptocurrencies—a strategy known as a "currency‑devaluation trade."
In fact, the dollar index fell almost 1% last week while gold and cryptocurrencies rose. Both assets continued to climb this week, but their gains were modest compared with the dollar’s strength.
The Canadian dollar was hit hard by the trade dispute and fell sharply this week.
Among other major currencies, the Canadian dollar drew attention from FX traders as the trade war between Washington and Ottawa heated up, leading the loonie to drop 1%.

After negotiations between the U.S. and Canada broke down over the weekend, both sides imposed retaliatory tariffs on each other. U.S. President Trump pushed on Thursday to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America."

Canadian government data released on Friday showed the economy rebounded strongly in the second quarter, growing 3.3% year‑over‑year, well above the revised 0.3% gain in the first quarter. The growth matched economists’ forecasts but far exceeded the Bank of Canada’s roughly 2.5% projection.
The yen touched 160 for the first time since the historic intervention.

Following Warsh’s hawkish speech, the yen came under pressure on Friday. USD/JPY reached 160, the first time it has hit that level since the historic joint U.S.–Japan intervention at the end of July. The 160 mark has previously been a trigger for intervention.

Conversely, the Korean won strengthened against the dollar for the second consecutive trading day, with USD/KRW falling about 0.5% this week. After investors digested the Bank of Korea’s decision on Thursday to raise rates for the second consecutive meeting, the won rallied and borrowing costs rose to an 18‑month high.

items.title_en: Was the U.S. Really Saving the Yen to Save Itself? Bessent Reveals the Hidden Motive
paras: 美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)為上月罕見出手支撐日元辯護，表示日元若出現失序波動，可能迫使投資人解除部位、衝擊全球金融市場，最終推高美國利率及家庭與企業的借貸成本。
貝森特在8月27日回覆民主黨參議員華倫(Elizabeth Warren)的信函中指出，日本是美債主要持有國，日元市場劇烈震盪可能引發強制平倉，進而造成全球市場動盪。他周五(28日)在社群平台X公開這封信。
美國財政部7月底與日本聯手買進日元，為1998年以來首次採取此類行動。市場觀察人士認為，貝森特之所以罕見介入匯市，除了支撐日元，也可能是為了防止日本出售美債籌措干預資金，導致美債殖利率進一步攀升。日本目前是美國公債最大的海外持有國。
貝森特沒有透露美國此次投入的具體金額，僅表示財政部動用外匯穩定基金(ESF)既有的外幣資產買進日元。他本月初曾透露，財政部在行動中使用歐元。日本財務省周五公布，政府過去一個月共投入創紀錄的964億美元支撐日元。
參議院銀行委員會民主黨首席議員華倫先前要求貝森特說明，財政部動用ESF干預日元的分析依據及法律基礎。
貝森特回應，財政部完全遵循ESF相關法規，法律明確授權財政部長在總統批准後進行外匯交易，以維持有秩序的匯率安排。他並強調，美國並未向日本提供信貸，「日本不欠財政部任何款項，因此也不存在日本無法償還債務的風險，因為這筆債務根本不存在。」
儘管美日聯手干預一度推升日元，相關漲幅目前已部分回吐。日元周五再次跌破1美元兌160日元，為兩國協調干預當日以來首見，顯示日元貶值壓力仍未消退。
paras_en: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended his rare intervention last month to support the yen, warning that a disorderly yen decline could force investors to unwind positions, shock global financial markets, and ultimately push up U.S. interest rates as well as borrowing costs for households and businesses.

In a letter to Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren dated August 27, Bessent noted that Japan is a major holder of U.S. Treasury debt and that severe yen market turbulence could trigger forced liquidations, further destabilizing global markets. He posted the letter publicly on X on Friday, the 28th.

At the end of July, the U.S. Treasury and Japan jointly bought yen – the first such coordinated action since 1998. Market observers say Bessent’s unusual foray into the FX market was not only to prop up the yen but also to prevent Japan from selling U.S. Treasuries to raise intervention funds, which could drive Treasury yields higher. Japan remains the largest foreign holder of U.S. government bonds.

Bessent did not disclose the exact amount the United States spent, only stating that the Treasury used foreign‑currency assets from the Exchange Stabilization Fund (ESF) to purchase yen. Earlier this month he revealed that the Treasury employed euros in the operation. Japan’s Finance Ministry announced on Friday that the government had injected a record $96.4 billion over the past month to support the yen.
Senate Banking Committee Democratic Chairman Elizabeth Warren had previously asked Bessent to explain the analytical and legal basis for the Treasury’s use of the ESF to intervene in the yen market.

Bessent responded that the Treasury fully complied with ESF statutes, which clearly authorize the Treasury Secretary, after presidential approval, to conduct foreign‑exchange transactions to maintain an orderly exchange‑rate arrangement. He emphasized that the United States has not extended any credit to Japan, saying, “Japan owes the Treasury nothing, so there is no risk of Japan being unable to repay debt because that debt simply does not exist.”

Although the joint U.S.–Japan intervention briefly lifted the yen, the gains have since been partially erased. The yen fell below ¥160 per dollar again on Friday – the first drop since the coordinated intervention – indicating that downward pressure on the currency remains.
